subject: Droki’s passage

subject: Emergence of Shal
fact: The arrival of Shal as the Deep King’s advisor triggered a rapid deterioration in the ruler’s mental state and control over the Underdark. This event marks the point where order began to unravel, and the corruption from the blackest depths began to manifest as physical madness, demonic incursions, and the collapse of the Deep King’s authority.
source_quote: “Ever since they became friends, the Deep King has been unwilling to listen to any sage advice.”

subject: Faerzress Anomaly
fact: A few months ago, the Faerzress — the magical radiation that suppresses teleportation and planar travel in the Underdark — glowed intensely, then dimmed and returned brighter than before. This event coincided with Buppido’s descent into divine madness and Pelek’s death. It is suspected to have caused a temporary rupture in planar boundaries, possibly allowing extraplanar entities or effects to bleed into the Underdark. The cause and nature of the event remain unknown.
source_quote: I did notice that the Faerzress glowed brightly, and after that, Buppido’s temperament changed. He became convinced he was some kind of divine figure.

subject: Faerzress anomaly
fact: The Faerzress glowed brightly, then went dark and returned brighter than before, altering Buppido’s temperament and possibly enabling planar breaches.
source_quote: I did notice that the Faerzress glowed brightly, and after that, Buppido’s temperament changed. He became convinced he was some kind of divine figure... It was almost as if it was being sucked out, and went dark and then came back brighter than before.

subject: Faerzress blink
fact: A phenomenon where the Faerzress glowed brightly, then darkened, and returned brighter than before; coincided with Buppido’s descent into divine delusion and Pelek’s death; suspected to have disrupted planar boundaries.
source_quote: I did notice that the Faerzress glowed brightly, and after that, Buppido’s temperament changed. He became convinced he was some kind of divine figure. ... It was almost as if it was being sucked out, and went dark and then came back brighter than before.

subject: Faerzress Fluctuation
fact: A recent and unprecedented event in which the Faerzress glowed intensely, dimmed, then returned brighter than before. This coincided with Buppido’s descent into delusional divinity and may have triggered planar instability. It is the central anomaly linking the murder, the madness, and the potential breach between planes.
source_quote: The Faerzress glow was unmistakable. It was almost as if it was being sucked out, and went dark and then came back brighter than before.

subject: Freezing the Lake

subject: ghostly possession avoidance

subject: ghostly time perception

source_quote: I don’t know... Less than a year? Telling time in this cavern is hard. And being unable to move more than 30 feet from your bones makes it harder. And as a ghost, the usual time markers don’t apply.

subject: Great Sundering
fact: The Great Sundering ended the era when gods could walk freely in Faerûn, triggering a collapse in divine access and prompting desperate magical attempts to manifest deities and demonic forces. This event is the root cause of the current surge in demonic activity, the failure of divine magic, and the rise of rituals like those of Tiamat and the Faerzress-driven madness.
source_quote: “The end of the great sundering ended the era that allowed the gods to walk in Faerûn freely.”

source_quote: My father was always very jealous, and there was always an undercurrent of hurt and shame in my name and how it affected my parents.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek laughed and said, 'Overbrighters.'
source_quote: Overbrighters.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek looked into the crack and described a tiny tunnel, then noticed Pygmywort and Bigwig.
source_quote: A tiny tunnel. Tiny all the way through. Oh, look at that Pygmywort and Bigwig.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek mentioned a family ring on his hand, an obsidian ring of some value.
source_quote: There is a family ring on it, an obsidian ring of some value.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek noticed the Faerzress glowed brightly and then went dark before returning brighter than before.
source_quote: I did notice that the Faerzress glowed brightly, and after that, Buppido’s temperament changed... It was almost as if it was being sucked out, and went dark and then came back brighter than before.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek recalled his childhood was delightful except for the emotional turmoil tied to his name.
source_quote: I had a delightful childhood, except when it came to my name.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek said Buppido killed him and cut his body into pieces he now sees.
source_quote: He killed me and cut my body up into the pieces you see here.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek said the hissing was just wind through the fungal thicket and called them 'Overbrighters' contemptuously.
source_quote: There’s nothing psychedelic about that sound. It’s the normal effect of wind blowing through a fungal thicket. ... Overbrighters.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek said to avoid anything on their person that counts to eight.
source_quote: Just don’t have anything on your person that counts - obviously - to eight.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek shrugged and said he didn’t know how long he’d been there, but less than a year.
source_quote: Less than a year? Telling time in this cavern is hard.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek’s ghostly head popped up and asked, 'He’s dead?'
source_quote: ‘He’s dead?’

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek’s ghostly head rolled into place and said, 'Wonderful!'
source_quote: ‘Wonderful!’

subject: Pelek becomes a merchant
fact: Pelek became a merchant and befriended Buppido due to family conflict and emotional neglect tied to his name.
source_quote: I suppose that’s why I ended up as a merchant, and became friends with Buppido and ignored the tell-tale signs of his incipient murderous rampage.

subject: Pelek explains his family history
fact: Pelek recounts his family’s conflict over his name, his mother’s choice of naming him after an actor, his father’s jealousy, and how this shaped his path to becoming a merchant and friend to Buppido.
source_quote: My mother named me after an actor. And well, there was always this doubt about the origin of the name and my lineage, which created a lot of friction in my family. And since you asked. I had a delightful childhood, except when it came to my name. My father was always very jealous, and there was always an undercurrent of hurt and shame in my name and how it affected my parents. I suppose that’s why I ended up as a merchant, and became friends with Buppido and ignored the tell-tale signs of his incipient murderous rampage.

subject: Pelek floats over bones
fact: Pelek’s ghost floats over his own dismembered remains and points to them, requesting they be collected and taken to Blingdenstone.
source_quote: The ghosts floats over some bones and points at them, “These bones are my bones, and I would appreciate you folks collecting my bones and bringing them to Blingdenstone.”

subject: Pelek laughs at 'Overbrighters'
fact: Pelek repeatedly uses the term 'Overbrighters' to dismiss the party’s concerns; his laughter and condescension irritate Thorin and unnerves Daz.
source_quote: The ghost laughs. “Overbrighters.” ... The ghost then, as politely and contemptuously as possible, says, “Overbrighters.”

subject: Pelek mentions his childhood
fact: Pelek describes his childhood as delightful except for the emotional turmoil surrounding his name and his father’s jealousy.
source_quote: I had a delightful childhood, except when it came to my name. My father was always very jealous, and there was always an undercurrent of hurt and shame in my name and how it affected my parents.

subject: Pelek says he doesn’t know how long he’s been dead
fact: Pelek admits he cannot accurately measure time since his death, as ghosts lack normal time markers and are confined to 30 feet from his bones.
source_quote: I don’t know,” he shrugs his shoulders, and his head flops off. He sighs apologetically, puts his head back on his neck, and continues, “Less than a year? Telling time in this cavern is hard. And being unable to move more than 30 feet from your bones makes it harder. And as a ghost, the usual time markers don’t apply.

subject: Pelek says he is a ghost
fact: Pelek repeatedly acknowledges his state as a ghost, describing his limitations and frustrations.
source_quote: And as a ghost, the usual time markers don’t apply." ... "I don’t want to possess you. It’s awkward.

subject: Pelek says he is a merchant
fact: Pelek states that he became a merchant after his family conflict, and that this led him to partner with Buppido.
source_quote: I suppose that’s why I ended up as a merchant, and became friends with Buppido...

subject: Pelek says he is delighted by Thorin’s ‘Classic Buppido’
fact: Pelek laughs in delight when Thorin says ‘Classic Buppido,’ indicating he recognizes and enjoys the dwarf’s dry humor.
source_quote: Thorin sighs, “Classic Buppido.” The ghost is delighted, “Yes! He killed me and cut my body up into the pieces you see here.”

subject: Pelek says he is fixated on stopping being a ghost
fact: Pelek admits to Thorin that his primary obsession as a ghost is to stop being one, making his struggle harder.
source_quote: And when you are a ghost, it’s a bit harder, what with my fixation on stopping being a ghost?

subject: Pelek says he likes the party
fact: Pelek tells the party he likes them and does not wish to possess them, calling possession awkward.
source_quote: Look, I don’t want to possess you. It’s awkward. And frankly, I like you.

subject: Pelek says he was a supplier
fact: Pelek identifies himself as Buppido’s supplier, essential to the smuggling operation despite his death.
source_quote: He needed a supplier who could act. And well, you know, that tickled me pink.

subject: Pelek says he was killed and dismembered
fact: Pelek confirms that Buppido killed him and cut his body into pieces, which now lie scattered in the cavern.
source_quote: He killed me and cut my body up into the pieces you see here.

subject: Pelek says he was stuck
fact: Pelek says he has been stuck in Grygum since his death, unable to move beyond 30 feet from his bones.
source_quote: And I have been stuck here ever since.

subject: Pelek says he was surprised he died
fact: Pelek expresses surprise at his own death, implying he did not expect to be killed by Buppido.
source_quote: I was surprised.

subject: Pelek says he was tickled pink
fact: Pelek describes his initial reaction to Buppido’s smuggling scheme as being “tickled pink,” indicating he was amused and eager to participate.
source_quote: And well, you know, that tickled me pink.

subject: Pelek says the Faerzress is unknown
fact: Pelek admits that no one knows what the Faerzress is, and he assumed its glow was just part of the Underdark’s nature.
source_quote: No one knows what the Faerzress is. And so I assumed it was something that happens.

subject: Pelek’s ghost merges into the rock
fact: Pelek’s ghost merges into the rock to peer through the crack in the wall and reports seeing a tunnel; he identifies the mushrooms on either side.
source_quote: The ghost sighs, “A tiny tunnel. Tiny all the way through.” Then the ghost pauses, “Oh, look at that Pygmywort and Bigwig.”

subject: Pelek’s Head Falls Off
fact: Pelek’s head flops off his body during a moment of apology, then he calmly puts it back on. This grotesque but routine behavior underscores his ghostly nature and detachment from physical norms.

subject: Pelek’s head flops off
fact: Pelek’s ghostly head repeatedly flops off his neck; he apologizes and reattaches it each time, a recurring physical trait.
source_quote: He sighs apologetically, puts his head back on his neck, and continues, ... his head flops off. ... puts his head back on.

subject: Pelek’s name origin ambiguity
fact: Pelek’s name’s origin is uncertain, tied to an actor he never met, and his family’s doubts about his lineage created lasting emotional conflict.
source_quote: There was always this doubt about the origin of the name and my lineage, which created a lot of friction in my family.

subject: planar breach hypothesis
fact: Daz hypothesizes that the Faerzress blink may have broken the walls between the planes, allowing Abyssal entities to enter.
source_quote: Then if it blinked, could it have - I dunno - broken the walls between the planes?

subject: spell failure
fact: Multiple spell attempts, including 'Tasha's Caustic Brew' and others, fail to impede the centipede swarm despite direct targeting.
source_quote: the centipedes somehow manage to avoid the brunt of the spell.

subject: swarm strike
fact: Thorin manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.
source_quote: Thorin actually manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.

subject: The Corruption of the Deep King
fact: The Deep King’s descent into paranoia and isolation began when he befriended the advisor Shal, who cut him off from sage counsel and accelerated the collapse of order in the Underdark city.
source_quote: Ever since they became friends, The Deep King has been unwilling to listen to any sage advice.

subject: The Escape from Laduguer’s Furrow
fact: The abandoned Duergar guardhouses along Laduguer’s Furrow were repurposed as observation posts by Buppido and Grygum to track Droki’s movements, revealing the historical liberation of Derro by Tarngardt and the lingering tension between the races.
source_quote: The duergar built a series of guardhouses to keep an eye on their derro slaves living in the West Cleft. These were abandoned when Deepking Tarngardt, grandfather of the current monarch, who liberated the derro, allowing them to spread from the West Cleft District into the East Cleft District.

subject: The Great Sundering
fact: The Great Sundering ended the era when the gods could walk freely in Faerûn, triggering a collapse in divine access and enabling unnatural demonic incursions into the material plane.
source_quote: The end of the great sundering ended the era that allowed the gods to walk in Faerûn freely.

subject: The Revelation of the Stonespeaker Crystal
fact: Hgraam’s gift of the stonespeaker crystal revealed that the Stone Giants possess knowledge of divine magic beyond mortal understanding and are willing to aid those who heed the stones’ warnings.
source_quote: “This is the stonespeaker crystal, with it you can cast Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, and Speak with Plants. It will also help you cast divinations.”

subject: The Rise of Buppido’s Shrine
fact: Buppido transformed from a captive Derro into a self-proclaimed prophet who constructed a bone altar in the caves and began demanding worship, believing his divine mission was being fulfilled.
source_quote: I didn’t expect you to find me here, with my shrine nearly finished! And power! My faithful are finally honoring me!

subject: The Sundering of the Gods' Presence
fact: The end of the great sundering ended the era when gods could walk freely in Faerûn. This event forced cults like the Cult of Tiamat to perform extraordinary rituals to manifest their deities in the material plane. The current proliferation of demons and madness is a direct consequence of this cosmic shift, suggesting a new, powerful magical force is destabilizing reality.
source_quote: The end of the great sundering ended the era that allowed the gods to walk in Faerûn freely. It’s why the Cult of Tiamat had to resort to such an extraordinary ritual to bring her into the prime material plane. That so many demons are walking freely is not normal. There is some kind of powerful magic that has enabled this.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asked if the ring was magical.
source_quote: Is the ring magical?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin charges forward and lands a solid blow on one of Buppido’s skeletons.
source_quote: Thorin, eager as ever, wastes no time. The dwarf charges forward, closing with one of the skeletons.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin draws his sword as Buppido becomes a direct threat.
source_quote: Thorin has his sword drawn.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin growled, 'It wasn’t powerful enough to keep you alive.'
source_quote: It wasn’t powerful enough to keep you alive.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin learns from Hgraam that the best way to the Dreamlands is through the city of the Deep gnomes.
source_quote: Thorin learns from Hgraam that the best way to the Dreamlands is through the city of the Deep gnomes.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembers that Stone Giants are not to be rushed into a conversation.
source_quote: Thorin remembers that Stone Giants are not one to be rushed into a conversation.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin shouted, 'Now listen here!' to Pelek.
source_quote: Now listen here!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin slapped Daz’s back in a friendly manner.
source_quote: Thorin slaps his back. A friendly slap on the back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin understands that the Duergar would have to go through the Derro to reach the tunnels, triggering a bloodbath.
source_quote: Thorin also understands why they are underneath the city. To get to the tunnels, the Duergar would have to go through the Derro, and that would trigger a bloodbath.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin warned the party that some mushrooms may have psychedelic effects and suggested holding their breath.
source_quote: there are some kinds of mushrooms that may have a psychedelic effect so I would hold our breath.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin whispers, 'If you betray us, I will gut you.'
source_quote: Thorin whispers, 'If you betray us, I will gut you.'

subject: Thorin asks how to avoid the number eight
fact: Thorin asks Pelek how to avoid the number eight, and Pelek replies with a simple directive: don’t have anything on your person that counts to eight.
source_quote: How do you avoid the number eight? ... Just don’t have anything on your person that counts - obviously - to eight.

subject: Thorin confronts Pelek
fact: Thorin confronts Pelek for offering no reward for retrieving his bones; demands to know if the ring is magical; receives a sarcastic response and is told to avoid references to Lolth, Menzoberranzan, the number eight, and spiders.
source_quote: Is the ring magical? ... No. But if I said otherwise, would it encourage you more? ... make sure to deny any association to Lolth, or Menzoberranzan, and make any references to the number eight or spiders.

subject: Thorin demands cooperation
fact: Thorin shouts at Pelek, demanding to know if they can work together and if he will help collect his bones, after the ghost has made no offer of aid.
source_quote: Now, can we work together, and will you collect my bones?

subject: Thorin sighs at Pelek
fact: Thorin sighs repeatedly in frustration at Pelek’s lack of utility and his bizarre, self-absorbed storytelling.
source_quote: Thorin sighs, “Classic Buppido.” ... Thorin sighs. ... Thorin growls, ... Thorin mutters, ...

subject: Thorin smashes the wall
fact: Thorin declares he will smash through the crack in the wall, but Zalthir stops him, insisting on silence due to nearby enemies.
source_quote: Thorin marches past Zalthir, ‘I am going to smash our way through.” Zalthir stops him. He thinks, “We must be quiet. There are many enemies about.”

subject: Thorin’s realization about Deep King’s police
fact: Thorin deduces that the Deep King uses secret invisible police to control the city, causing opposition to flee underground.
source_quote: The Deep King has relied on his secret invisible police to control the city, and so opposition has gone underneath it.

subject: Thorin’s threat to Buppido
fact: Thorin whispers a threat to Buppido if he betrays them after freeing him.
source_quote: If you betray us, I will gut you.

subject: Thorin takes mental notes
fact: Thorin documents Pelek’s claims about the Faerzress and the Underdark’s changes, concluding that the ghost has offered no useful information and demands better cooperation.
source_quote: He takes mental notes: "He’s confirmed that something weird has happened in the Underdark, and that it’s connected to the Faerzress. But I knew that. And it’s not like he’s given us any useful information. Time for this to change.”

subject: Toll the Dead Fails
fact: Daz casts 'Toll the Dead' against centipede swarms, hoping to kill them. The creatures save successfully, leaving Daz stunned and despairing. His magic is powerless against their resilience.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: turn undead
fact: Grygum successfully cast Turn Undead against Buppido’s skeleton minions, overwhelming them with divine power and turning the battle into a slaughter.
source_quote: The cleric’s words of power overwhelm the skeletal minions of Buppido.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir notices the stark contrast between the clean Duergar dwellings and the cluttered Derro slums.
source_quote: The contrast with the clean, perfect Duergar dwellings is obvious.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes the Derro slums are dirty and cluttered, with homes carved into walls and piled atop one another.
source_quote: The district's dirty and cluttered streets clearly formed as dwellings spread and came together, not as a product of planning.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir plunges the cavern into darkness to disrupt the skeletons.
source_quote: Zalthir, never one to shy away from unusual tactics, plunges the area into darkness.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized the Derro ate mushrooms and saw a crack in the wall too small to fit through.
source_quote: The Derro ate some mushrooms. ... The crack is too small for anyone to fit into.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, 'We must be quiet. There are many enemies about.'
source_quote: We must be quiet. There are many enemies about.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, 'What we have seen as localized appearances of demons is not localized.'
source_quote: So what we have seen as localized appearances of demons is not localized.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir stumbled, unable to remember the vague teachings of his monastic order after the ghost’s banter.
source_quote: he mutters and stumbles, unable to remember the appropriately vague and incomprehensible teaching of his monastic order

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought, 'This place used to be where hippies hid out. Now it has become a den of vipers aimed at the mad Deepking.'
source_quote: This place used to be where hippies hid out. Now it has become a den of vipers aimed at the mad Deepking.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir’s darkness disrupts the skeletons, causing some to blunder blindly.
source_quote: Confusion reigns for a moment. Some of the skeletons blunder blindly in the darkness, stumbling around aimlessly.

subject: Zalthir is quiet
fact: Zalthir remains silent throughout the party’s interactions with Pelek and Daz’s actions, offering no commentary.
source_quote: As for Zalthir, Zalthir is quiet.

subject: Zalthir reflects on ormu
fact: Zalthir compares Nightlights unfavorably to ormu, a mushroom that can be crushed into a paste for light, lamenting the inefficiency of the former.
source_quote: It is so unlike the ormu,” he reflects on silently. “That can be crushed into a paste and used as a light source. Not the Nightlight.

subject: Zalthir’s darkness
fact: Zalthir plunges the cavern into darkness to disorient undead and disrupt Buppido’s control.
source_quote: Zalthir, never one to shy away from unusual tactics, plunges the area into darkness.

subject: Zalthir’s observation of Derro slums
fact: Zalthir observes the Derro slums and concludes why non-Duergar are needed to navigate them safely.
source_quote: And now, why Errde Blackstaff and the Keeper of the Flames were so anxious to find a non-Duergar to come here is clear.

subject: Zalthir’s reflection on Stone Giants
fact: Zalthir reflects that the Stone Giants’ patience and subtlety may offer lessons to his monastic order.
source_quote: Perhaps there is something that even his monastic order could learn from their subtlety and patience.

subject: Zalthir stumbles over monastic teachings
fact: Zalthir is mentally overwhelmed by the party’s banter and cannot recall his monastic order’s vague teachings, which were meant to refocus his attention.
source_quote: he stumbles, unable to remember the appropriately vague and incomprehensible teaching of his monastic order to refocus his attention after enduring the endless banter between the ghost, the dwarf, and the orc.

subject: Zalthir throws punches at centipedes
fact: Zalthir reacts to the centipede swarm by throwing punches at them, which Daz perceives as brave or reckless.
source_quote: Zalthir is quick to act, throwing punches at one of the swarms. "Brave," Daz thinks, "or reckless."

subject: Zalthir wonders about monastic silence spells
fact: Zalthir reflects on his monastic training, wishing he had learned spells to make people silent rather than blind.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders why a monastic order devoted to silence only taught him how to make people blind, and not how to make them silent.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: A faction of derro led by Buppido, involved in smuggling goods out of the city to avoid Duergar taxes; Pelek was their supplier; Droki is a messenger for them.
source_quote: He was working with a faction of Derro known as the Council of Savants. ... The derro messenger? No. I was told that he works for the Council of Savants.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is a Derro intellectual order that promised liberation and enlightenment to the Derro people but failed to deliver, leading to widespread disillusionment and radicalization. Buppido and others now view them as traitors, and their broken promises have fueled the rise of cultic movements and violent dissent within the Derro community.
source_quote: “The Council of Savants will fail my people. I must go and save them!”

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is a Derro organization operating in the Underdark. It is involved in smuggling, arcane research, and possibly planar manipulation. Buppido and Droki are affiliated with it. The Council is suspected of exploiting the Faerzress anomaly and may be responsible for inducing madness in its members through exposure or ritual.
source_quote: He was working with a faction of Derro known as the Council of Savants.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is a Derro organization that promised freedom to the Derro but failed to deliver, leading to Buppido’s radicalization and his belief in a divine mission to save his people.
source_quote: He screams about the Council of Savants who promised freedom and failed to deliver freedom. ... The Council of Savants will fail my people. I must go and save them!

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is a derro governing body that promised freedom to the Derro but failed to deliver it, inciting deep rage and betrayal among those like Buppido who still believe in their divine mission.
source_quote: He screams about the Council of Savants who promised freedom and failed to deliver freedom.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is a faction of derro operating in the Underdark, known for their scholarly yet mad pursuits. They are involved in smuggling and subterfuge, and Buppido was an agent working with them. They are connected to Droki, the derro messenger, who is said to be peculiar and possibly mad. The Council is suspected of exploiting the Faerzress anomaly for unknown purposes.
source_quote: Buppido said he could move product out of the city without dealing with the Duergar taxes.

subject: Cult of Tiamat
fact: The Cult of Tiamat is a demonic sect that resorted to an extraordinary ritual to bring Tiamat into the prime material plane due to the loss of divine accessibility after the end of the great sundering.
source_quote: The end of the great sundering ended the era that allowed the gods to walk in Faerûn freely. It’s why the Cult of Tiamat had to resort to such an extraordinary ritual to bring her into the prime material plane.

subject: Cult of Tiamat
fact: The Cult of Tiamat resorted to an extraordinary ritual to manifest the Dragon Queen into the Prime Material Plane after the end of the Great Sundering ended the era when gods could walk freely in Faerûn. Their actions are part of a larger pattern of desperate, high-stakes magic attempting to bypass divine restrictions, suggesting a hidden force—possibly tied to the Faerzress or the stonespeaker crystal—is enabling such incursions.
source_quote: “It’s why the Cult of Tiamat had to resort to such an extraordinary ritual to bring her into the prime material plane.”

subject: Deep Gnomes (Svirfneblin)
fact: The Deep Gnomes, who dwell in the city beneath Gracklstugh, are the only faction trusted to navigate the Dreamlands safely. Hgraam confirms that their city is the correct path, validating Jimjar’s claims. They are likely maintaining a fragile neutrality between the Duergar, Derro, and other Underdark powers, and may be the key to understanding the spreading madness and the nature of the evil stirring below.
source_quote: “The best way to the Dreamlands is through the city of the Deep gnomes.”

subject: Deep King’s Court
fact: The Deep King’s Court is the ruling authority of the Underdark city, now corrupted by the advisor Shal, struggling to maintain order as chaos seeps upward from the Underdark and downward from the surface.
source_quote: The Deep King has tried to keep order and control, and the more he trie,s the more the order escapes and tries to take the city from him.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a broken, scattered people living in chaotic, overcrowded burrows beneath Gracklstugh, ruled by madness and ritual. They are exploited by the Duergar, betrayed by the Council of Savants, and now being drawn into cultic worship led by figures like Buppido. Their tunnels are used by Droki to move unseen between factions, and their collective insanity may be a symptom of a deeper magical corruption spreading from the Underdark.
source_quote: “The chatter in the air is unnerving, with hundreds of derro muttering, screaming at each other, and otherwise reveling in their insanity.”

subject: Derro
fact: The derro once used a network of tunnels through the whorlstone, as mentioned by Buppido and later confirmed by Pelek. Their historical presence implies prior exploitation of the area’s magical geography and fungal resources.

subject: Derro Community
fact: The Derro community is a fractured, insane population living in squalor beneath Gracklstugh, marked by paranoia, violence, and chaotic muttering; they harbor burning hatred toward outsiders and are ruled by no central authority, only fragmented rituals and rumors.
source_quote: The chatter in the air is unnerving, with hundreds of derro muttering, screaming at each other, and otherwise reveling in their insanity.

subject: Duergar
fact: A subterranean dwarf race that imposes taxes on trade in the Underdark; Buppido claimed he could bypass their levies.
source_quote: Buppido said he could move product out of the city without dealing with the Duergar taxes.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a dwarven subrace who once enslaved the Derro, building guardhouses to monitor them in the West Cleft; they were later overthrown by Deepking Tarngardt, who liberated the Derro and allowed them to spread into the East Cleft District.
source_quote: The duergar built a series of guardhouses to keep an eye on their derro slaves living in the West Cleft. These were abandoned when Deepking Tarngardt, grandfather of the current monarch, who liberated the derro, allowing them to spread from the West Cleft District into the East Cleft District.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a subterranean dwarven people who impose taxes on trade and movement through their territories in the Underdark. Buppido and Pelek sought to bypass their tolls using the Council of Savants’ network. Their presence is a constant economic and political pressure in the region.
source_quote: Buppido said he could move product out of the city without dealing with the Duergar taxes.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a subterranean dwarven race that controls taxation and trade routes in the Underdark. Buppido sought to evade their levies by using Grygum as a supplier and later eliminating him. Their presence is a constant pressure on Derro smuggling operations, and their influence extends into the political and economic structure of the region.
source_quote: He needed to move product out of the city without dealing with the Duergar taxes.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar maintain strict control over Gracklstugh, enforcing segregation between their clean, geometric dwellings and the squalid Derro slums. They abandoned the guardhouses once used to monitor Derro slaves after Tarngardt I liberated them. Now they are caught between internal decay, the Deep King’s unraveling, and the rising demonic incursions, yet remain outwardly rigid and oppressive.
source_quote: “The duergar built a series of guardhouses to keep an eye on their derro slaves... abandoned when Deepking Tarngardt... liberated the derro.”

subject: Monastic Order of Silence
fact: A monastic order devoted to silence has trained Zalthir exclusively in making others blind, not in inducing silence — a profound mismatch that troubles him and suggests a deeper, unspoken agenda or corruption in their teachings.

subject: Svirfneblin
fact: The Svirfneblin (deep gnomes) traditionally name themselves after objects or sounds associated with them, often using onomatopoeia, as evidenced by Pelek’s naming convention.
source_quote: The Gnomes tend to name themselves after things and that many of their names are onomatopoeia of the sounds of those things.

subject: The Deep Gnomes
fact: The Deep Gnomes are a reclusive, magically attuned race ruled by the Deep King, who struggles to maintain order as corruption from the Underdark infiltrates their city. They are caught between Duergar control above and Derro chaos below, relying on invisible enforcers to suppress dissent — a strategy that has pushed opposition underground.
source_quote: The Deep King has tried to keep order and control, and the more he tries, the more the order escapes and tries to take the city from him.

subject: The Derro
fact: The Derro are a degenerate, chaotic subterranean race living in filthy, unplanned burrows and ramshackle structures. Their slums are dangerous and hostile, marked by deep resentment toward the Duergar. Their role as couriers for multiple factions stems from their isolation and the necessity of navigating between hostile territories.
source_quote: The Derro slums are dangerous to anyone. Even from here, it’s evident that the homes of the Derro are mostly burrows carved into the walls and simple structures piled atop one another. The district's dirty and cluttered streets clearly formed as dwellings spread and came together, not as a product of planning.

subject: The Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a reclusive, rigidly orderly subterranean race whose meticulously clean city borders the chaotic Derro slums. Their strict control over movement and access, enforced by badges of the Stone Guard, creates a stark contrast with the unruly Derro districts. They avoid direct conflict with the Derro due to the risk of triggering a bloodbath.
source_quote: From Themberchaud’s cave to the Cairngorm Cavern, Thorin and his friends must traverse through the city of Duergar, where no one but the Duergar is allowed. But the badges of the Keepers of the Flame or Stone Guard are enough to stop anyone from asking too many questions.

subject: Blingdenstone
fact: A gnomish city in the Underdark; Pelek’s goal is to have his bones transported there; it is described as the party’s exit route to the Overbrite.
source_quote: I need a favor.” The ghosts floats over some bones and points at them, “These bones are my bones, and I would appreciate you folks collecting my bones and bringing them to Blingdenstone.” ... The city of Blingdenstone is your exit.

subject: Blingdenstone route
fact: Blingdenstone is the exit point for the party, accessible via multiple routes from the Underdark.
source_quote: The city of Blingdenstone is your exit. There are many routes to the Overbrite from there.

subject: Buppido’s shrine
fact: A macabre altar of bones and skeletons arranged in a spiral pattern, tended by a deranged cultist named Buppido.
source_quote: cluster of skeletons around Buppido... arranged in a spiral pattern around the cave’s center

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: A vast, ancient cavern located beyond Themberchaud’s cave, home to Hgraam and the Stone Giants. It is connected to the city of Duergar via a gigantic tunnel in the eastern wall south of Laduguer’s Furrow. The cavern is polished, serene, and deeply resonant with the magic of the earth.
source_quote: From Themberchaud’s cave to the Cairngorm Cavern, Thorin and his friends must traverse through the city of Duergar... A long tunnel opens in the eastern wall south of Laduguer’s Furrow. The tunnel is gigantic, even by the massive size of Gracklstugh. And the rock is well polished. And sitting on a rock is a very large and very venerable stone giant.

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Cairngorm Cavern is the origin point of Zalthir’s journey to Laduguer’s Furrow.
source_quote: From the Cairngorm Cavern, Laduguer’s Furrow is just a short distance

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Cairngorm Cavern is the starting point for journeys to Laduguer’s Furrow and the Derro slums.
source_quote: From the Cairngorm Cavern, Laduguer’s Furrow is just a short distance

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: The Cairngorm Cavern is the entrance to the Deep King’s domain, connected to Laduguer’s Furrow, and marked by colossal stone structures and polished rock surfaces.
source_quote: From Themberchaud’s cave to the Cairngorm Cavern, Thorin and his friends must traverse through the city of Duergar... A long tunnel opens in the eastern wall south of Laduguer’s Furrow. The tunnel is gigantic, even by the massive size of Gracklstugh. And the rock is well polished.

subject: Cairngorm Cavern
fact: The ancient cavern where Hgraam resides, located near the edge of Gracklstugh’s Duergar district. It is a place of deep geological resonance, where the stones speak and the giant listens. The cavern is a sanctuary of patience and ancient wisdom, and the only place in the Underdark where truth is spoken slowly and deliberately.
source_quote: “The giant stands up, looks at Daz, ‘You are too hasty. And I have rocks to tend to.’”

subject: Cavern of Bones
fact: A cavern carpeted with humanoid remains arranged in a spiral, where Buppido has built his shrine.
source_quote: floor is carpeted with humanoid remains in varying stages of decomposition, arranged in a spiral pattern around the cave’s center

subject: Cavern of Bones
fact: A dark, confined cavern where Grygum’s bones lie, and where he has been bound as a ghost for less than a year. The space is too small to move beyond 30 feet from the bones, and time is difficult to measure here. It is the site of his murder and the origin point of the party’s current quest. The walls are silent, and the air carries the scent of old earth and decay.
source_quote: Being unable to move more than 30 feet from your bones makes it harder.

subject: Cavern of Decomposing Remains
fact: A hidden cavern southwest of the main entrance, carpeted with humanoid corpses arranged in a spiral, humming with an off-key tone from a hunched figure; its purpose is unknown but suggests ritualistic or sacrificial practices by an unknown entity.
source_quote: The floor is carpeted with humanoid remains in varying stages of decomposition, arranged in a spiral pattern around the cave’s center. An off-key humming comes from a hunched figure working busily at something on the floor.

subject: Cavern of Whispering Echoes
fact: A cavern where the sound of dripping water makes no echo, suggesting magical dampening or distortion.
source_quote: the dripping of water makes no echo, as if Daz stood in open air

subject: caves
fact: The battle occurred in a cave system that previously housed Buppido’s shrine of bones and skeletons, now littered with the remains of the derro and his undead servants.
source_quote: The blood-spattered remains of Buppido lie scattered amongst the bones that made up the crazed Derro’s hideout.

subject: cave with pool of water
fact: To the northeast of the cave entrance is a cave with a pool of water, unexplored by the party.
source_quote: To the northeast is a cave with a pool of water.

subject: Cave with Pool of Water (Northeast)
fact: A cave located to the northeast of the entrance, containing a pool of water. Its significance is unknown, but it may be a resting point, ritual site, or source of information. Zalthir noted its presence as he returned to the entrance to reorient himself after the ghost’s revelations.
source_quote: To the northeast is a cave with a pool of water.

subject: centipedes
fact: The centipedes keep coming, relentless and unsettling.
source_quote: the centipedes keep coming, relentless and unsettling.

subject: combat zone
fact: The combat zone is characterized by a relentless swarm of centipedes, ongoing spellcasting attempts, and visible frustration from the party.
source_quote: The centipedes keep coming, relentless and unsettling.

subject: crack in wall with mushroom trail
fact: A crack in the wall, flanked by Pygmywort and Bigwig mushrooms, leads to a tiny tunnel only accessible by ghostly perception.
source_quote: A well-trodden path ends at a crack in the wall, with mushrooms to either side of the crack... Oh, look at that Pygmywort and Bigwig.

subject: Deep King’s Citadel
fact: The Deep King’s citadel is the seat of power where paranoia has taken root since Shal’s arrival.
source_quote: The Deep King has been unwilling to listen to any sage advice.

subject: Deep King’s domain
fact: The Deep King rules from a city where order escapes as control increases, and evil permeates below.
source_quote: The Deep King has tried to keep order and control, and the more he trie,s the more the order escapes and tries to take the city from him.

subject: Derro City (Gracklstugh)
fact: Derro City is a sprawling, chaotic settlement carved into the rock beneath Gracklstugh, where homes are crude holes in walls, the air reeks of decay, and the population is driven mad by isolation and oppression; its streets are patrolled by muttering derro who react with violent hatred to outsiders.
source_quote: The stench in the air changes from acrid and metallic to fetid and repugnant... The homes in this part of Gracklstugh are crudely carved from the rock or are just holes in the walls, arranged in no apparent order.

subject: Derro Slums
fact: A chaotic, filthy district of burrows and stacked structures, formed organically by unregulated expansion. The slums are dangerous, hostile, and filled with resentment toward the Duergar. Their lack of planning and cleanliness contrasts violently with the Duergar’s rigid order, making them a breeding ground for rebellion and covert operations.
source_quote: The Derro slums are dangerous to anyone. Even from here, it’s evident that the homes of the Derro are mostly burrows carved into the walls and simple structures piled atop one another. The district's dirty and cluttered streets clearly formed as dwellings spread and came together, not as a product of planning.

subject: Derro slums
fact: The Derro slums are a chaotic, unplanned district of burrows and piled structures, reeking of squalor and madness.
source_quote: homes... mostly burrows carved into the walls and simple structures piled atop one another... dirty and cluttered streets... formed as dwellings spread and came together

subject: Derro’s tunnels
fact: The Derro tunnels are accessed only by bypassing Duergar-controlled routes, as direct passage triggers bloodshed.
source_quote: To get to the tunnels, the Duergar would have to go through the Derro, and that would trigger a bloodbath.

subject: Droki’s Path
fact: Droki’s path is a well-worn trail marked by dropped junk, making him predictable and reliable for faction couriers.
source_quote: Droki's path is very well worn and marked with junk that the Derro drops.

subject: Droki’s trail
fact: Droki’s trail leads from the cave entrance through the fungal thicket and across the frozen lake, marked by consistent footprints and mushroom consumption.
source_quote: To the north is another cave and the obvious trail of Droki... Droki’s obvious trail... Droki’s trail is on the other side of the lake.

subject: Duergar city
fact: Duergar city is a place of rigid order where only Duergar are permitted, contrasting with the chaos of Derro districts.
source_quote: where no one but the Duergar is allowed

subject: East Cleft District
fact: East Cleft is the expanded territory of the liberated Derro, now densely populated and chaotic.
source_quote: allowing them to spread from the West Cleft District into the East Cleft District

subject: Faerzress-affected Zone
fact: A region where the Faerzress distorts perception and sanity, casting spiral patterns and muting sound.
source_quote: The glow of faerzress casts an eerie soft light... swirling into spiral patterns... the sound around you is strangely muted

subject: Faerzress Cavern
fact: A long cavern lined with stalactites and stalagmites, where water drips silently and faerzress casts eerie spiral light.
source_quote: long cavern lined with stalactites and stalagmites... glow of faerzress casts an eerie soft light... swirling into spiral patterns... the dripping of water makes no echo

subject: Fungal Thicket
fact: A dense wall of fungi five feet tall, blocking the eastern tunnel juncture. It emits a hissing, whispering sound from wind passing through perforated caps, mistaken for voices. The thicket contains numerous magical fungi, including Nightlights, Devil’s Mushrooms, Torchstalks, and more.

subject: Ghohlbrorn’s Lair
fact: Ghohlbrorn’s Lair is where Buppido was held captive and where Jimjar plays games of chance.
source_quote: head back to Ghohlbrorn’s Lair, where they find Jimjar playing a game of chance

subject: Ghohlbrorn’s Lair
fact: Ghohlbrorn’s Lair is where Jimjar plays games of chance and Buppido is held captive before his escape.
source_quote: head back to Ghohlbrorn’s Lair, where they find Jimjar playing a game of chance

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cavernous derro hideout located beneath the Underdark, where Buppido’s corpse and Pelek’s scattered bones lie. It is filled with bones, fungi, and magical mushrooms, including Pygmywort, Bigwig, Nightlights, torchstalk, timmask, and barrelstalk. A narrow tunnel behind a crack in the wall leads to unknown regions. The area is haunted by Pelek’s ghost and is the site of recent planar instability.
source_quote: The blood-spattered remains of Buppido lie scattered amongst the bones that made up the crazed Derro’s hideout.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cavernous hideout of the derro Buppido, scattered with bones and the remains of his dismembered partner Pelek; the walls contain a crack too small for passage, flanked by Pygmywort and Bigwig mushrooms; a thermal lake with black water lies to the northeast; a fungal thicket with hissing fungi blocks the eastern tunnel.
source_quote: The blood-spattered remains of Buppido lie scattered amongst the bones that made up the crazed Derro’s hideout. A crack in the wall, with mushrooms to either side of the crack. The crack is too small for anyone to fit into. A large pool filling the cavern ahead, stretching nearly one hundred feet to the opposite shore. The most striking feature of this pool is its unnervingly black water. A dense fungi forest. The path ahead vanishes into a thicket where the tallest specimens reach about five feet, creating a wall of fungal life that requires effort to pass through.

subject: Hgraam’s cave
fact: Hgraam’s cave is the dwelling of the ancient stone giant who speaks in riddles and bestows the stonespeaker crystal.
source_quote: he heads back into his cave

subject: Laduguer’s Furrow
fact: A clean, geometric corridor separating the Duergar district from the Derro slums. Its spotless design contrasts violently with the chaos of the West Cleft. It is a symbolic boundary—between order and madness, between oppressor and oppressed. The abandoned guardhouses along it serve as observation points, and its entrance is the threshold to the Derro’s hidden world.
source_quote: “Looking around, he notices how this is so spotlessly clean in its style.”

subject: Laduguer’s Furrow
fact: A meticulously clean, narrow corridor in the Duergar city, flanked by entrances leading to the Derro slums. It serves as a stark boundary between order and chaos, cleanliness and filth, control and anarchy. The contrast highlights the deep societal fractures in the Underdark.
source_quote: From the Cairngorm Cavern, Laduguer’s Furrow is just a short distance. Looking around, he notices how this is so spotlessly clean in its style. At either edge of this Furrow is an entrance. And past that entrance, he can see a slum.

subject: Laduguer’s Furrow
fact: Laduguer’s Furrow is a clean, orderly corridor separating Duergar territory from Derro slums, with abandoned guardhouses.
source_quote: Laduguer’s Furrow is just a short distance... abandoned guardhouses now stand empty

subject: Laduguer’s Furrow
fact: Laduguer’s Furrow is a clean, orderly corridor with entrances on either side, contrasting sharply with the Derro slums to the west.
source_quote: at either edge of this Furrow is an entrance... spotlessly clean in its style

subject: Laduguer’s Furrow
fact: Laduguer’s Furrow is a pristine, orderly Duergar thoroughfare flanked by entrances leading to the Derro slums, and it contrasts sharply with the chaotic, cluttered West Cleft District.
source_quote: From the Cairngorm Cavern, Laduguer’s Furrow is just a short distance. Looking around, he notices how this is so spotlessly clean in its style. At either edge of this Furrow is an entrance. And past that entrance, he can see a slum.

subject: Laduguer’s Furrow
fact: Laduguer’s Furrow is the western gate of a dwarven-underdark complex, historically used by Duergar to control Derro movement; now a point of entry into the Derro slums and the hidden caverns beyond, it is a place of transition and danger.
source_quote: He leads them to the western gate of Laduguer’s Furrow.

subject: Main Cavern with Faerzress Glow
fact: A vast, silent cavern lined with stalactites and stalagmites, illuminated by the eerie soft glow of faerzress; the air is metallic, sounds are muffled, and the dripping water echoes nowhere, suggesting a magical or otherworldly property.
source_quote: The glow of faerzress casts an eerie soft light across this cavern... The dripping of water makes no echo, as if Daz stood in open air.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is referenced as a Drow city that enslaves similarly to the Duergar, prompting moral reflection.
source_quote: how the Drow of Menzoberranzan do it

subject: Northern Cavern (Droki’s Trail)
fact: A narrow, winding cavern leading from the main cave, marked by Droki’s unmistakable trail. It ends at a crack in the wall too small for passage, flanked by mushrooms that Droki consumed. The crack suggests a hidden mechanism, illusion, or biological adaptation. Zalthir has identified the trail and the mushrooms, but cannot determine how to proceed.
source_quote: A well-trodden path ends at a crack in the wall, with mushrooms to either side of the crack.

subject: overbrite access route
fact: Blingdenstone provides access to the Overbrite, a location the party must reach to continue their journey.
source_quote: The city of Blingdenstone is your exit. There are many routes to the Overbrite from there.

subject: Spidersilk Caves
fact: The Spidersilk Caves are a site of demonic presence, noted as one of many non-localized demonic manifestations.
source_quote: the Beholder in the Spidersilk caves

subject: The Black Pool
fact: A vast, underground lake in Grygum, filled with unnervingly black, thermal water that hides unknown entities beneath its surface. The water is warm due to a thermal spring. Daz froze the surface with magic to allow the party to cross. It lies at the end of a sloping tunnel and marks the boundary between the derro lair and the fungal thicket beyond.
source_quote: This is no mere puddle but a large pool filling the cavern ahead, stretching nearly one hundred feet to the opposite shore. The most striking feature of this pool is its unnervingly black water.

subject: the crack in the wall
fact: A narrow fissure in the cavern wall, flanked by Pygmywort and Bigwig mushrooms; too small for passage; Pelek’s ghost can see through it and reports a tiny tunnel.
source_quote: A crack in the wall, with mushrooms to either side of the crack. The crack is too small for anyone to fit into. ... A tiny tunnel. Tiny all the way through.

subject: The Fungal Thicket
fact: A dense, towering forest of fungi east of the Black Pool, blocking the path forward. It is alive with hissing sounds caused by wind passing through perforated mushrooms. It contains numerous magical fungi: Pygmywort, Bigwig, Nightlights, torchstalk, timmask, barrelstalk, and others. It is infested with swarms of centipedes. The thicket is a natural barrier and a source of both sustenance and danger.
source_quote: Blocking the tunnel juncture is a dense fungi forest. The path ahead vanishes into a thicket where the tallest specimens reach about five feet, creating a wall of fungal life that requires effort to pass through.

subject: the fungal thicket
fact: The fungal thicket east of the lake is a dense wall of fungi five feet tall, emitting a hissing sound from wind passing through perforated mushrooms; it contains Nightlights, barrelstalk, bluecap, ripplebark, trillimac, waterorb, zurkwhood, timmask, torchstalk, and swarms of centipedes.
source_quote: A hissing sound begins to rise. It sounds like uncounted tiny voices whispering in tongues he doesn't understand. ... Nightlights—mushrooms that grow to 15 feet and shed light in a 15-foot-by-15-foot circle. ... barrelstalk, a large, cask-shaped fungus that stores water, bluecap for making flour, ripplebark that tastes good toasted, trillimac that can be used for scrolls and makes a bread-like substance that can be rolled up, waterorb for storing water, and zurkwhood for making things. ... a two-foot-tall toadstool with orange and red stripes across its beige cap known as “the devil’s mushroom,” or a timmask. ... a two-foot-tall mushroom ... known as torchstalk. ... swarms of them.

subject: Themberchaud’s cave
fact: Themberchaud’s cave is the origin point of Thorin’s journey toward the Cairngorm Cavern.
source_quote: From Themberchaud’s cave to the Cairngorm Cavern

subject: the northern cavern
fact: A cavern accessed from Grygum, containing Droki’s trail and the crack in the wall; Zalthir investigates it after abandoning the ghostly dialogue.
source_quote: To the north is another cave and the obvious trail of Droki. ... Zalthir walks into the northern cavern and sees Droki’s obvious trail.

subject: the Overbrite
fact: A region beyond Blingdenstone; Pelek says it is the party’s exit from the Underdark; access requires avoiding references to Lolth, Menzoberranzan, the number eight, and spiders.
source_quote: The city of Blingdenstone is your exit. There are many routes to the Overbrite from there. And to help you a little bit, when you get there, make sure to deny any association to Lolth, or Menzoberranzan, and make any references to the number eight or spiders.

subject: thermal lake
fact: A vast, black, heated pool fills the cavern, stretching nearly 100 feet to the opposite shore, frozen by Daz’s spell.
source_quote: This is no mere puddle but a large pool filling the cavern ahead, stretching nearly one hundred feet to the opposite shore. The most striking feature of this pool is its unnervingly black water... the water is surprisingly heated by a thermal spring...

subject: the thermal lake
fact: A vast underground lake stretching nearly one hundred feet across, with unnervingly black, opaque water heated by a thermal spring; Daz froze it with magic to allow passage.
source_quote: A large pool filling the cavern ahead, stretching nearly one hundred feet to the opposite shore. The most striking feature of this pool is its unnervingly black water. ... the water is surprisingly heated by a thermal spring, making it pleasantly warm to his touch.

subject: the whorlstone tunnels
fact: A network of tunnels referenced by Buppido as a route used by derro; Pelek mentions them as part of the derro’s smuggling paths.
source_quote: Buppido mentioned that there were tunnels that the derro used to go through the whorlstone tunnels.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a vast, evil-infested realm where madness creeps from the blackest depths and the rock itself cries in pain.
source_quote: Something evil stirs in the Underdark. The rock itself cries in pain and horror, and a madness creeps from the blackest depths.

subject: underdark fungal thicket
fact: A dense fungal thicket blocks the tunnel juncture east of the lake, emitting a hissing whisper from wind through perforated mushrooms.
source_quote: Blocking the tunnel juncture is a dense fungi forest... a hissing sound begins to rise. It sounds like uncounted tiny voices whispering in tongues he doesn't understand.

subject: Underdark Lake
fact: A vast, 100-foot-wide pool of unnervingly black, thermal-heated water, hidden in a cavern. Daz freezes its surface with magic, allowing the group to cross via ice blocks. The lake is a key waypoint between the crack and the fungal thicket.

subject: Valkenvylve
fact: Valkenvylve is a location where demons have appeared, part of a pattern of widespread demonic incursions.
source_quote: The demons at Valkenvylve

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: West Cleft
fact: West Cleft is a Derro district where Droki’s hidden entrance lies, and where Buppido’s shrine is later found.
source_quote: stops between a cluster of hovels in West Cleft

subject: West Cleft
fact: West Cleft is a derro-controlled district within Gracklstugh, once monitored by Duergar guardhouses; now abandoned, it serves as a labyrinth of hovels and hidden passages, including the secret fissure accessed by Droki, and is the epicenter of derro madness and ritual movement.
source_quote: Droki stops between a cluster of hovels in West Cleft and turns... revealing a narrow fissure in the chasm wall.

subject: West Cleft District
fact: The West Cleft District is a squalid, unstructured Derro slum carved into the rock walls, filled with muttering, insane inhabitants, and marked by filth, decay, and open hostility toward outsiders.
source_quote: The homes in this part of Gracklstugh are crudely carved from the rock or are just holes in the walls, arranged in no apparent order. The chatter in the air is unnerving, with hundreds of derro muttering, screaming at each other, and otherwise reveling in their insanity. Those who spot Grygum look at him with a burning hatred.

subject: West Cleft District
fact: The slum district of Gracklstugh where the Derro live in squalor, carved into the rock with no planning or order. It is a place of hatred, madness, and hidden power. The abandoned Duergar guardhouses overlook it, and the hidden fissure used by Droki leads from here into the deeper tunnels. It is the epicenter of Buppido’s cult and the point where the corruption of the Underdark becomes visible in physical form.
source_quote: “The homes in this part of Gracklstugh are crudely carved from the rock or are just holes in the walls, arranged in no apparent order.”

subject: West Cleft District
fact: West Cleft is a former slave district, now abandoned guardhouses serve as vantage points overlooking Derro territory.
source_quote: The duergar built a series of guardhouses to keep an eye on their derro slaves living in the West Cleft. These were abandoned when Deepking Tarngardt... liberated the derro

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: A network of tunnels beneath Gracklstugh used by Droki to transport messages between factions. It is a neutral zone where even enemies trust Droki to pass safely. The caverns are likely tied to the Dreamlands and may be a conduit for the spreading madness or a prison for something ancient. The fact that even the Deep King’s agents use it suggests it is older than the current powers.
source_quote: “Droki can be trusted to deliver messages to the groups in the Whorlstone caverns and keep secrets.”

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: The Whorlstone Caverns are a hidden network accessible only through secret passages in the Derro slums, used by Droki as a secure courier route trusted by all factions.
source_quote: Droki can be trusted to deliver messages to the groups in the Whorlstone caverns and keep secrets. ... He steps over the moldy boxes, and jumps into the crack. Just as he disappears into the cavern, a wisp of eerie fog floats out.

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: Whorlstone Caverns are a secret network accessible only through hidden fissures in West Cleft, used by Droki.
source_quote: Droki is someone all of the factions trust and can get to the Whorlstone Caverns safely

subject: Whorlstone Caverns access
fact: A secret fissure behind moldy boxes and canvas in West Cleft leads to the Whorlstone Caverns, marked by eerie fog.
source_quote: lifts the scrap of cloth, pushes the gray sheets of canvas to the side, revealing a narrow fissure... a wisp of eerie fog floats out

subject: Whorlstone Tunnels
fact: A network of subterranean tunnels once traversed by the derro, now partially blocked by fungal growths. The tunnels lead to a vast underground lake and are associated with magical mushrooms and ghostly echoes.

subject: whorlstone tunnels
fact: The derro used hidden tunnels through the whorlstone, mentioned by Buppido as part of their smuggling network.
source_quote: Buppido mentioned that there were tunnels that the derro used to go through the whorlstone tunnels.

subject: centipedes
fact: Centipedes are swarming relentlessly, avoiding spell effects despite targeted attempts, and continuing to move with unsettling persistence.
source_quote: The centipedes somehow manage to avoid the brunt of the spell.

subject: centipedes
fact: Swarms of centipedes that emerge in the fungal thicket; resistant to Toll the Dead and Tasha's Caustic Brew; they swarm over Zalthir and cause deep unease in Daz.
source_quote: swarms of them. ... Daz watches as the centipedes emerge, a shiver running down his spine. ... the centipedes somehow manage to avoid the brunt of the spell.

subject: centipedes
fact: The centipedes are relentless and unsettling, continuing to come despite being struck.
source_quote: the centipedes keep coming, relentless and unsettling.

subject: Centipede Swarms
fact: Massive, numerous swarms of centipedes that emerge unexpectedly from the fungal thicket. They are unaffected by Daz’s 'Toll the Dead' spell, indicating high resistance to necrotic magic. Their presence ruins Daz’s delight in the fungi.

subject: Centipede Swarms
fact: Swarm-sized centipedes infest the fungal thicket, emerging when the party moves through the area. They are resistant to both 'Toll the Dead' and 'Tasha's Caustic Brew', suggesting unusual resilience, possibly due to planar corruption or innate Underdark adaptation. They are aggressive and capable of swarming targets, causing distress and physical danger.
source_quote: The centipedes, now emboldened, began to swarm over Zalthir.

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Demonic Entities Across the Underdark
fact: A surge of demonic presence — including the demons at Valkenvylve, the Beholder in the Spidersilk Caves, the demonic manta rays, and Demogorgon — is not coincidental. These are manifestations of a larger, systemic magical corruption in the Underdark, enabled by an unknown force that has broken natural barriers between planes.
source_quote: What we have seen as localized appearances of demons is not localized. The demons at Valkenvylve, the Beholder in the Spidersilk caves, the demonic manta rays, and Demogorgon, all of this is no coincidence.

subject: demonic manifestations
fact: Demons at Valkenvylve, the Beholder in Spidersilk Caves, demonic manta rays, and Demogorgon are not localized but part of a coordinated resurgence.
source_quote: The demons at Valkenvylve, the Beholder in the Spidersilk caves, the demonic manta rays, and Demogorgon, all of this is no coincidence.

subject: Derro
fact: Derro are insane, subterranean humanoids who live in chaotic, unstructured slums, exhibit violent paranoia, and are feared and despised by both Duergar and surface dwellers.
source_quote: The chatter in the air is unnerving, with hundreds of derro muttering, screaming at each other, and otherwise reveling in their insanity. Those who spot Grygum look at him with a burning hatred.

subject: Droki
fact: A derro messenger for the Council of Savants; known for being peculiar and possibly mad; leaves a clear trail through the caverns, leading to a crack in the wall and through the fungal thicket.
source_quote: The derro messenger? No. I was told that he works for the Council of Savants. He’s very peculiar. Some say he’s mad. ... the obvious trail of Droki. ... Droki’s obvious trail. ... Droki’s trail is on the other side of the lake.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a Derro courier whose unnaturally fast pace and ritualistic muttering make him a trusted and invisible conduit between factions, and whose path through the slums is the only safe route to the Whorlstone Caverns.
source_quote: He mutters a repetitive series of phrases at different volumes... Droki also doesn’t seem to care if anyone is following him. ... Droki wanders between the various houses and merchants of the Derro, as if there is no purpose to his walking.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a derro messenger affiliated with the Council of Savants. He is described as peculiar, possibly mad, and follows habitual patterns. His trail leads from Buppido’s lair through the fungal thicket, past the Black Pool, and into unknown tunnels. He is likely aware of the Faerzress anomaly and may be acting on orders from the Council.
source_quote: He works for the Council of Savants. He’s very peculiar. Some say he’s mad.

subject: Faerzress
fact: The Faerzress is an enigmatic magical phenomenon in the Underdark, associated with planar instability, teleportation denial, and madness. It recently underwent a dramatic fluctuation — glowing brightly, dimming, then returning brighter — which coincided with Buppido’s descent into delusional divinity. Its nature is unknown, but its behavior suggests it may be a sentient or semi-sentient force tied to the boundaries between planes.
source_quote: No one knows what the Faerzress is.

subject: Hunched Figure in Spiral Cavern
fact: An unidentified, possibly derro or twisted entity, hunched over a spiral of decomposing remains, emitting an off-key hum; its actions suggest ritualistic necromancy or sacrificial work, and it remains unaware of intruders.
source_quote: An off-key humming comes from a hunched figure working busily at something on the floor.

subject: skeletons
fact: A cluster of animated skeletons served Buppido as minions, were marked by Fairie Fire, and were later destroyed by Grygum’s Turn Undead after being disoriented by Zalthir’s darkness.
source_quote: Three skeletons are marked, and an ethereal glow surrounds them.

subject: stone giant presence
fact: A very large and very venerable stone giant sits on a rock near Laduguer’s Furrow.
source_quote: sitting on a rock is a very large and very venerable stone giant

subject: Stone Giants
fact: Stone Giants are ancient, slow-speaking beings attuned to the rocks, who perceive the pain of the Underdark and speak in cryptic portents, and are capable of wielding divine insight and magical artifacts.
source_quote: The giant stares at him. And then raises an eyebrow. ... “Something evil stirs in the Underdark. The rock itself cries in pain and horror, and a madness creeps from the blackest depths.”

subject: swarms
fact: One of the swarms was struck with a significant blow by Thorin.
source_quote: Thorin actually manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido believes he is on a divine mission to save his people.
source_quote: The divine mission requires that I go back! I must go and save them!

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido is a Derro who murdered and dismembered Grygum, his former supplier, to eliminate competition and gain control over smuggling routes. He is tied to the Council of Savants and sought to bypass Duergar taxes. He experienced a sudden shift in perception after the Faerzress glowed and dimmed, becoming convinced of his own divinity. His actions and mental state are central to the unfolding mystery.
source_quote: He promised to prove his point and brought me here.

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido is a Derro who once served as a courier but has since descended into fanatical madness, believing himself a divine prophet and constructing a shrine of humanoid remains in the caverns beneath the West Cleft. He claims to be fulfilling a divine mission to save his people from the Council of Savants, yet he has already committed murder and now seeks worshipers. He is capable of teleportation or rapid displacement between locations, suggesting magical or planar interference. He is both a threat and a potential key to understanding the Derro’s spiritual corruption.
source_quote: “The divine plan tells me I must help you!”

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido is a derro who was imprisoned but freed by Grygum; he knows Droki intimately, is enraged by the broken promises of the Council of Savants, and believes in a divine mission to save his people.
source_quote: I have to get back to save my people. The divine mission requires that I go back! The Council of Savants will fail my people. I must go and save them!

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido was a derro merchant who partnered with Pelek, worked with the Council of Savants, and claimed he could move product out of the city without dealing with the Duergar taxes; he became convinced he was a divine figure after the Faerzress glowed and then darkened.
source_quote: He was working with a faction of Derro known as the Council of Savants. Buppido said he could move product out of the city without dealing with the Duergar taxes. And well, he needed a supplier who could act. And well, you know, that tickled me pink. He promised to prove his point and brought me here.

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido was a derro who believed himself divine after the Faerzress glowed and dimmed. He was a business partner of Pelek and worked with the Council of Savants to smuggle goods out of the Underdark without paying Duergar taxes. He killed and dismembered Pelek, scattering his bones. His transformation coincided with an unusual Faerzress event. He is now dead, his corpse found in the derro hideout.
source_quote: He promised to prove his point and brought me here.

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido was a derro who manifested a macabre shrine of bones and skeletons, claimed divine authority over faithful followers, and attacked with manic violence before being slain by Daz's magic missiles.
source_quote: Your divine mission is now over.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz identified the torchstalk as a mushroom with a combustible cap that burns for 24 hours.
source_quote: Why, that’s a torchstalk. It has a combustible cap and can burn for 24 hours when lit.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a contemplative observer who reflects on the systemic cruelty of slavery across races, particularly comparing Duergar and Drow practices; he tracks Droki’s path and enters a horrifying cavern filled with decomposing remains and an unknown humming figure.
source_quote: Free people are the basis of any society.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow mage deeply fascinated by Underdark fungi, trained to recognize their magical properties. He enthusiastically collects and identifies fungi, casts spells with flair, and is unnerved by the auditory effects of the fungal thicket. His spell 'Toll the Dead' fails against centipede swarms, leaving him shaken.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an arcane spellcaster who recognized Buppido’s threat, cast Fairie Fire to mark skeletons for advantage, and ultimately killed Buppido with Magic Missile, ending the battle.
source_quote: Magic missiles," he thinks, visualizing the shimmering darts.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an orc who observes and reacts to the ghost’s revelations with curiosity. He is the one who proposes the theory that the Faerzress’s blink may have broken planar boundaries. His insight is met with skepticism by the ghost, but he remains engaged in the mystery, prompting Grygum to reveal further details about the obsidian ring and the hand.
source_quote: Then if it blinked, could it have — I dunno — broken the walls between the planes?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is impulsive and inquisitive, frequently interrupting solemn revelations with blunt questions. His inquiry about what is driving everyone mad triggered a profound response from Hgraam. He is hopeful and persistent, seeking direct answers even when the universe offers riddles.
source_quote: Do you know what’s driving everyone mad?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is plagued by a lingering sense of doubt about his spell choices.
source_quote: Daz finds himself scanning his spell list, second-guessing his choices

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is scanning his spell list, second-guessing his choices, feeling unease about spell effectiveness, and scratching at his arms due to phantom bug sensations despite knowing none are present.
source_quote: Maybe 'Burning Hands' would have been better? ... He keeps scratching at his arms, feeling the phantom sensation of bugs despite knowing there were none on him.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is second-guessing his spell choices, considering 'Burning Hands' or a wider-area spell, and feels unease over perceived spell ineffectiveness.
source_quote: Daz finds himself scanning his spell list, second-guessing his choices. 'Maybe 'Burning Hands' would have been better?' he muses, or perhaps something with a wider area of effect. He feels a slight unease, wondering if his spells are just ineffective or if he needs to re-strategize.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz perks up as Thorin strikes the swarm, scans his spell list, second-guesses his choices, and muses that 'Burning Hands' would have been better or perhaps something with a wider area of effect.
source_quote: Daz perks up as Thorin actually manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow. "Yes! There you go!" he thinks, a glimmer of hope returning. ... Daz finds himself scanning his spell list, second-guessing his choices. "Maybe 'Burning Hands' would have been better?" he muses, or perhaps something with a wider area of effect.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized Nightlights as mushrooms that glow in a 15-foot circle and stop glowing when touched or cut.
source_quote: Nightlights—mushrooms that grow to 15 feet and shed light in a 15-foot-by-15-foot circle. When they are touched or cut, they stop glowing.

subject: Deep King Tarngardt II
fact: The current ruler of Gracklstugh, son of the liberator Tarngardt I, who once freed the Derro from Duergar oppression. Now he is a broken, paranoid figure, manipulated by Shal, whose attempts to maintain order have only accelerated the collapse of control beneath the city. His mental state has deteriorated to the point of rejecting allies and ignoring the cries of the earth.
source_quote: “The more he tries, the more the order escapes and tries to take the city from him.”

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a Derro courier trusted by all factions in Gracklstugh due to his unnaturally fast, predictable, and seemingly oblivious movement through the city. He navigates the Derro slums and Underdark tunnels with eerie precision, carrying messages between the Whorlstone Caverns and various powers. He is not insane in the traditional sense—he is methodical, almost ritualistic, and may be under magical influence. He uses a hidden fissure behind a wall of rags and boxes to access the deeper tunnels.
source_quote: “Droki is late! They will be so angry! Stupid, stupid, stupid! Delays, blocks, procrastination, obstructions, pfah!”

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a Derro courier who operates across factional lines, surviving in the dangerous slums. His ability to move between hostile territories suggests he is either exceptionally skilled, deeply connected, or protected by forces unknown.
source_quote: Droki, he is told, is to the west.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a Derro messenger working for the Council of Savants. He is described as peculiar and possibly mad. His well-trodden trail leads to a narrow crack in the wall, flanked by mushrooms — which he consumed. His behavior suggests ritualistic or altered-state patterns, and his path may be the key to accessing hidden Derro sanctums or escape routes.
source_quote: The Derro is a creature of habit.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a courier trusted by all factions for safe passage through the Whorlstone Caverns.
source_quote: Droki can be trusted to deliver messages to the groups in the Whorlstone caverns and keep secrets.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a derro courier whose unnaturally fast pace and disregard for observation make him a trusted, if mysterious, messenger; he moves through Derro city with ritualistic repetition, delivering messages and accessing hidden routes, including a concealed fissure in the West Cleft.
source_quote: Droki is late! They will be so angry! Stupid, stupid, stupid! Delays, blocks, procrastination, obstructions, pfah! No time, no rhyme, not mine! No! Time!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes that the widespread presence of demons is enabled by powerful magic.
source_quote: There is some kind of powerful magic that has enabled this.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum casts 'Tasha's Caustic Brew' in response to the centipede swarm, but the spell fails to impede them.
source_quote: Grygum then steps up, casting 'Tasha's Caustic Brew.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who prepared to turn undead against Buppido’s skeletons, held his action due to Zalthir’s darkness, and later performed a ritual for Buppido’s soul.
source_quote: And as he prepares to pray for Buppido’s soul, a ghostly head pops up.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a ghost bound to a cluster of bones in a cavern, unable to move more than 30 feet from them. He was murdered and dismembered by Buppido, his former business partner. He seeks help transporting his bones to Blingdenstone and has revealed fragmented knowledge about the Faerzress anomaly and Derro madness.
source_quote: He was surprised. He doesn't know how long he's been here. Less than a year? Telling time in this cavern is hard.

subject: Grygum
