fact: Grygum is a quiet, insightful observer who connects cosmic events to current phenomena. He recognizes the significance of the Sundering and the unnatural proliferation of demons, suggesting an underlying magical force is destabilizing the fabric of reality.
source_quote: The end of the great sundering ended the era that allowed the gods to walk in Faerûn freely. It’s why the Cult of Tiamat had to resort to such an extraordinary ritual to bring her into the prime material plane. That so many demons are walking freely is not normal. There is some kind of powerful magic that has enabled this.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an impulsive dwarf who swallows magical mushrooms, shrinks, and cannot squeeze through cracks. He repeatedly exclaims 'Wow!' and is easily awed by magical displays, despite his own mishaps.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an orc determined to locate Droki and reach the Whorlstone Caverns, relying on Buppido’s knowledge and navigating Derro city with caution, aware of his ancestral enmity with dwarves and the volatile nature of the Derro.
source_quote: We need to get him to show us the way to the Whorlstone caverns. If we go around poking for things, it’s unclear what could happen.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a Stone Giant who speaks the wisdom of the stones, reveals that the Deep King has been corrupted by an advisor named Shal, and gifts the stonespeaker crystal to enable Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, Speak with Plants, and enhanced divinations.
source_quote: Hgraam sighs, “Yes, it was a tragedy. You did not try to kill him. But you did try to stop him. He was driven mad.” ... His assistant brings a 19 inch shard of quartz crystal. ... “This is the stonespeaker crystal, with it you can cast Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, and Speak with Plants. It will also help you cast divinations.”

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a venerable Stone Giant who resides in the Cairngorm Cavern, attuned to the deep rocks and aware of the corruption spreading through the Underdark. He serves as a reluctant oracle, offering cryptic warnings about evil’s presence and the Deep King’s descent into paranoia. He gifted the party the Stonespeaker Crystal and revealed that Shal, a new advisor, has corrupted the Deep King and refuses to meet anyone. He confirmed that the best path to the Dreamlands lies through the city of the Deep Gnomes, validating Jimjar’s claims.
source_quote: “Something evil stirs in the Underdark... By these portents, you shall know of evil’s presence and of evil’s face. This is what the stones tell me.”

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a venerable stone giant who resides in the Cairngorm Cavern and serves as a keeper of ancient rock wisdom. He is deeply attuned to the suffering of the Underdark and has witnessed the Deep King’s descent into paranoia. He gifted Thorin the Stonespeaker Crystal and revealed that Shal, a new advisor, has corrupted the Deep King’s judgment.
source_quote: Yes, it was a tragedy. You did not try to kill him. But you did try to stop him. He was driven mad. Something evil stirs in the Underdark. The rock itself cries in pain and horror, and a madness creeps from the blackest depths. Pay heed to the signs surrounding you. A cave with two faces. Rock devoured, and the land overgrown. The pebble believes itself flesh. The earth rejects its wards, and the tunnels shake in fury. By these portents, you shall know of evil’s presence and of evil’s face. This is what the stones tell me.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is attuned to the stones and speaks their wisdom.
source_quote: This is what the stones tell me.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is cryptic in the best of times.
source_quote: Stone Giants are cryptic in the best of times.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a figure whose claims about the route to the Dreamlands have been verified by Hgraam. His knowledge is trusted by Thorin, indicating he is a reliable source of subterranean lore.
source_quote: Thorin learns from Hgraam that the best way to the Dreamlands is through the city of the Deep gnomes. Thorin is pleased to have Jimjar's claims vetted.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek announced his name, 'Pelek, at your service if you will be at mine.'
source_quote: ‘Pelek, at your service if you will be at mine.’

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek became a merchant because of the emotional fallout from his name and his relationship with Buppido.
source_quote: I suppose that’s why I ended up as a merchant, and became friends with Buppido and ignored the tell-tale signs of his incipient murderous rampage.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek identified Pygmywort as a mushroom with a one-inch stem and blue cap with white dots that shrinks like a reduce spell.
source_quote: Pygmywort is the mushroom with a one-inch-long stem and a stubby blue cap with white dots, and Bigwig is the four-inch-tall mushroom with a thin stem and a wide purple cap. The first one shrinks you, like the effect of a reduce spell, and the latter grows you, like the effect of an enlarge spell.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a ghost whose mother named him after an actor, and whose father disliked the name, creating family friction; he was killed and dismembered by Buppido, and now seeks to have his bones taken to Blingdenstone; he wears an obsidian family ring on a lost hand.
source_quote: My mother named me after an actor. And well, there was always this doubt about the origin of the name and my lineage, which created a lot of friction in my family. And since you asked. I had a delightful childhood, except when it came to my name. My father was always very jealous, and there was always an undercurrent of hurt and shame in my name and how it affected my parents. I suppose that’s why I ended up as a merchant, and became friends with Buppido and ignored the tell-tale signs of his incipient murderous rampage.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a ghostly Svirfneblin merchant who was killed and dismembered by Buppido. His bones are scattered in the derro hideout. He claims his name was given by his mother after an actor, and his family history is fraught with shame and friction. He seeks to have his bones taken to Blingdenstone and offers cryptic advice about avoiding Lolth, Menzoberranzan, the number eight, and spiders. He is fixated on his ghostly state and his failed attempts at acting. He knows of the Council of Savants and Buppido’s plan to bypass Duergar taxes. He is aware of the Faerzress anomaly and its possible connection to planar instability.
source_quote: My mother named me after an actor. And well, there was always this doubt about the origin of the name and my lineage, which created a lot of friction in my family. And since you asked. I had a delightful childhood, except when it came to my name. My father was always very jealous, and there was always an undercurrent of hurt and shame in my name and how it affected my parents. I suppose that’s why I ended up as a merchant, and became friends with Buppido and ignored the tell-tale signs of his incipient murderous rampage.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a ghostly entity who speaks with polite contempt, corrects misconceptions about fungal sounds, and references entities like 'Overbrighters.' He has observed and commented on the magical properties of fungi and the behavior of the group.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is the ghostly Svirfneblin whose name is derived from an actor his mother named him after, causing familial shame and tension, and who was once a merchant and friend of Buppido.
source_quote: My mother named me after an actor.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek was a supplier for Buppido, who worked with the Council of Savants to move product past Duergar taxes.
source_quote: He was working with a faction of Derro known as the Council of Savants. Buppido said he could move product out of the city without dealing with the Duergar taxes.

subject: Shal
fact: Shal is a mysterious new advisor to the Deep King of the Deep Gnomes. Since their arrival, the Deep King has become paranoid, rejecting sage counsel and isolating himself. Hgraam has attempted to meet Shal but has been refused access, suggesting Shal wields covert influence over the Deep King’s decisions.
source_quote: Yes, Shal, an advisor of his. Ever since they became friends, The Deep King has been unwilling to listen to any sage advice. I have asked to meet Shal, but they refuse.

subject: Shal
fact: Shal is the mysterious advisor to the Deep King who has caused him to reject sage counsel and become paranoid, and whom Hgraam has tried and failed to meet.
source_quote: Yes, Shal, an advisor of his. Ever since they became friends, The Deep King has been unwilling to listen to any sage advice.” ... “I have asked to meet Shal, but they refuse.”

subject: Shal
fact: Shal is the mysterious new advisor to Deep King Tarngardt II, whose influence has caused the monarch to reject sage counsel, become paranoid, and lose control over the Underdark’s growing chaos. Hgraam has attempted to meet Shal but has been refused. Shal’s identity, origins, and nature remain unknown, but their arrival coincides with the Deep King’s unraveling and the surge of demonic incursions.
source_quote: “Ever since they became friends, the Deep King has been unwilling to listen to any sage advice.”

subject: The Deep King
fact: The Deep King is the ruler of the Deep Gnomes, once calm and wise, now consumed by paranoia. He has struggled to maintain order in his city as corruption from the Underdark spreads, and his reliance on an invisible police force has driven opposition underground. His transformation is directly tied to the influence of Shal.
source_quote: Many have told the Deep King that what goes underneath the city affects what goes on in his city. And what goes on in his city affects what goes on below. And much of what goes on below is evil. The Deep King has tried to keep order and control, and the more he tries, the more the order escapes and tries to take the city from him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin charged in and successfully struck one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.
source_quote: Thorin charges in, swinging with his weapon. Daz perks up as Thorin actually manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin charges in and successfully strikes one of the centipede swarms, dealing a significant blow, offering a moment of hope.
source_quote: Thorin charges in, swinging with his weapon. Daz perks up as Thorin actually manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin charges in, swinging with his weapon, and manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.
source_quote: Thorin charges in, swinging with his weapon. Daz perks up as Thorin actually manages to strike one of the swarms, dealing a significant blow.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt taken for granted and noted that Pelek had offered nothing in return for help.
source_quote: He’s confirmed that something weird has happened in the Underdark... But I knew that. And it’s not like he’s given us any useful information.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf deeply skeptical of Grygum’s requests. He resents being asked to carry bones without receiving aid or information in return. He has compiled mental notes on the Faerzress anomaly, Buppido’s ties to the Council of Savants, and the possibility of planar disruption. He is determined to extract useful intelligence and shift the dynamic from obligation to collaboration.
source_quote: This guy wants us to take his bones to Blingdenstone and hasn’t helped us. Time for this to change.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf warrior who charged into combat against Buppido’s skeletons, landed a solid blow on one, and later expressed sorrow over Buppido’s death despite the violence.
source_quote: He was a crazy one, but he was our crazy one.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf who offers cautious advice about psychedelic mushrooms, physically supports Daz with a slap on the back, and leads the group through the fungal thicket. He is pragmatic and responsive to environmental dangers.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a wary ally who distrusts Buppido after witnessing his past murder; he issues a direct threat of violence should Buppido betray them, yet permits his movement into the caverns.
source_quote: If you betray us, I will gut you.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin muttered, 'He was a crazy one, but he was our crazy one,' with sadness.
source_quote: ‘He was a crazy one, but he was our crazy one,’ mutters a sad Thorin.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir admires the stone giants’ subtlety and patience.
source_quote: They speak little. They ponder and then they consider their words.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a monk who admires the Stone Giants’ patience and subtlety. He is deeply observant and reflective, seeking to learn from their wisdom. He is now journeying to find Droki in the Derro slums, where he notes the stark contrast between Duergar order and Derro chaos.
source_quote: Zalthir likes the stone giants. They speak little. They ponder and then they consider their words. Perhaps there is something that even his monastic order could learn from their subtlety and patience.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a monk who has detached from the chaotic dialogue around the ghost and returned to the cave entrance to pursue the trail of Droki. He is methodical, attuned to environmental clues, and struggles to reconcile his monastic discipline with the absurdity of the party’s interactions. He has identified Droki’s trail, the mushroom-eaten crack in the wall, and the impossibility of passage — leading him to pause, while Thorin prepares to force entry.
source_quote: I don’t see how we go past this.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a silent observer who has been trained in magical fungi lore but not in silence, and is haunted by the failure of his spells against centipedes. He watches others act while internally questioning his purpose and training.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a tactician who used darkness to disorient Buppido’s undead minions, creating opportunity for allies, and supported Grygum’s plan by disrupting visibility.
source_quote: Zalthir plunges the area into darkness.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir urges caution throughout the mission, questioning the wisdom of trusting Buppido and moving into the Derro slums, yet remains an active participant in the group’s decisions.
source_quote: Zalthir urges caution, but Grygum is determined.

subject: Barrelstalk
fact: A large, cask-shaped fungus that stores water. Collected by Daz as a potential resource.
source_quote: barrelstalk, a large, cask-shaped fungus that stores water

subject: barrelstalk property
fact: Barrelstalk is a large, cask-shaped fungus that stores water.
source_quote: He picks up some barrelstalk, a large, cask-shaped fungus that stores water...

subject: Bigwig
fact: A mushroom with a four-inch-tall stem and a wide purple cap; when consumed, it causes an enlarge spell effect, growing the consumer.
source_quote: Pygmywort is the mushroom with a one-inch-long stem and a stubby blue cap with white dots, and Bigwig is the four-inch-tall mushroom with a thin stem and a wide purple cap. The first one shrinks you, like the effect of a reduce spell, and the latter grows you, like the effect of an enlarge spell.

subject: Bigwig
fact: A mushroom with a four-inch-tall thin stem and a wide purple cap. When consumed, it enlarges the eater as per an enlarge spell. Mentioned by ghosts and fungi experts, but not consumed by the group.

subject: bigwig effect
fact: Bigwig enlarges the consumer like an enlarge spell, with a four-inch stem and wide purple cap.
source_quote: Pygmywort is the mushroom with a one-inch-long stem and a stubby blue cap with white dots, and Bigwig is the four-inch-tall mushroom with a thin stem and a wide purple cap. ... the latter grows you, like the effect of an enlarge spell.

subject: Bluecap
fact: A mushroom used for making flour. Collected by Daz for future sustenance.

subject: bluecap
fact: A mushroom used for making flour; collected by Daz.
source_quote: bluecap for making flour

subject: bluecap property
fact: Bluecap can be used to make flour.
source_quote: He picks up some barrelstalk... bluecap for making flour...

subject: Buppido’s shrine
fact: Buppido’s shrine is a macabre altar constructed from humanoid bones and skeletons arranged in a spiral pattern, used to channel divine power and attract worshipers.
source_quote: The floor is carpeted with humanoid remains in varying stages of decomposition, arranged in a spiral pattern around the cave’s center. ... I didn’t expect you to find me here, with my shrine nearly finished!

subject: Burning Hands
fact: Daz muses that 'Burning Hands' would have been better or perhaps something with a wider area of effect.
source_quote: Maybe 'Burning Hands' would have been better?" he muses, or perhaps something with a wider area of effect.

subject: centipede resistance
fact: The centipedes are unusually resistant to necrotic and acid damage, suggesting magical or divine protection.
source_quote: the centipedes somehow manage to avoid the brunt of the spell... Were these bugs unusually lucky, under the protection of some bug god...

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants promised freedom to the Derro but failed to deliver, inciting rage and religious fervor.
source_quote: The Council of Savants who promised freedom and failed to deliver freedom... The Council of Savants will fail my people.

subject: crossbow
fact: One of Buppido’s skeletons used a crossbow to strike Grygum during the chaos of Zalthir’s darkness, inflicting a visible injury.
source_quote: One skeleton, however, manages to take a shot at Grygum with its crossbow.

subject: devil’s mushroom effect
fact: Timmask (devil’s mushroom) causes madness if uprooted, with orange and red stripes on a beige cap.
source_quote: Watch out," he shouts to Thorin. The dwarf was close to a two-foot-tall toadstool with orange and red stripes across its beige cap known as “the devil’s mushroom,” or a timmask. Uprooting the mushroom can cause madness.

subject: Devil’s Mushroom (Timmask)
fact: A two-foot-tall toadstool with orange and red stripes on a beige cap. Uprooting it causes madness. Daz warns Thorin about it, recalling his own past trauma from its effects.

subject: Droki’s Hidden Fissure Entrance
fact: A concealed entrance in the West Cleft, revealed by moving scraps of cloth, gray canvas, and moldy boxes; it leads into a narrow cavern where a wisp of eerie fog escapes upon entry, suggesting magical or extraplanar properties.
source_quote: Droki lifts the scrap of cloth, pushes the gray sheets of canvas to the side, revealing a narrow fissure... a wisp of eerie fog floats out.

subject: Droki’s path
fact: Droki’s path is a well-worn trail through the Derro slums marked with dropped junk, deliberately maintained to ensure his predictability and reliability as a courier.
source_quote: Droki's path is very well worn and marked with junk that the Derro drops. The Derro’s predictability is precisely why everyone uses him.

subject: hooked spear
fact: Buppido wielded a hooked spear in his final charge against Thorin, but his attack was wild and ineffective, driven by fury rather than skill.
source_quote: Buppido rushes at Thorin with a hooked spear but misses wildly.

subject: Nightlight
fact: A 15-foot-tall mushroom that emits a 15x15-foot circle of light. When touched or cut, it stops glowing. Daz identifies it as unlike the ormu, which can be crushed into a paste for light.

subject: nightlight property
fact: Nightlight mushrooms glow in a 15x15-foot radius and cease glowing when touched or cut, growing up to 15 feet tall.
source_quote: It is so unlike the ormu... Nightlights—mushrooms that grow to 15 feet and shed light in a 15-foot-by-15-foot circle. When they are touched or cut, they stop glowing.

subject: Nightlights
fact: Mushrooms growing up to 15 feet tall that emit light in a 15x15-foot circle; they stop glowing when touched or cut.
source_quote: Nightlights—mushrooms that grow to 15 feet and shed light in a 15-foot-by-15-foot circle. When they are touched or cut, they stop glowing.

subject: obsidian family ring
fact: An obsidian ring of value worn by Pelek on his lost hand; non-magical but potentially valuable; Pelek offers it as a reward if the hand is found.
source_quote: There is a family ring on it, an obsidian ring of some value. You can keep it if you find the hand.

subject: Obsidian Ring
fact: A family ring worn by Pelek, made of obsidian and of significant value. It is attached to his missing hand, which wandered off after his death. The ring is not magical, but Pelek implies it may be more valuable if claimed as such. It is a potential reward for retrieving his hand.
source_quote: There is a family ring on it, an obsidian ring of some value. You can keep it if you find the hand.

subject: Obsidian Ring
fact: An obsidian ring of value is attached to Grygum’s missing hand. It is not magical, but Grygum implies it may have been if it would motivate the party to find the hand. It is a personal artifact of his former life and may bear familial or symbolic significance.
source_quote: There is a family ring on it, an obsidian ring of some value. You can keep it if you find the hand.

subject: obsidian ring value
fact: An obsidian ring of some value is on Pelek’s hand, which may be recovered.
source_quote: There is a family ring on it, an obsidian ring of some value. You can keep it if you find the hand.

subject: Ormu
fact: A fungus that can be crushed into a paste to serve as a light source. Daz contrasts it unfavorably with Nightlights, which lose their glow when touched.

subject: phantom bug sensation
fact: Daz experiences a phantom sensation of bugs on his arms despite knowing none are present, and repeatedly scratches at his skin.
source_quote: He keeps scratching at his arms, feeling the phantom sensation of bugs despite knowing there were none on him.

subject: phantom sensation of bugs
fact: Daz keeps scratching at his arms, feeling the phantom sensation of bugs despite knowing there were none on him.
source_quote: He feels a slight unease, wondering if his spells are just ineffective or if he needs to re-strategize. All the while, he keeps scratching at his arms, feeling the phantom sensation of bugs despite knowing there were none on him.

subject: Pygmywort
fact: A mushroom with a one-inch-long stem and a stubby blue cap with white dots. When consumed, it shrinks the eater as per a reduce spell. Grygum swallowed it and became too small to fit through the crack.

subject: Pygmywort
fact: A mushroom with a one-inch-long stem and a stubby blue cap with white dots; when consumed, it causes a reduce spell effect, shrinking the consumer.
source_quote: Pygmywort is the mushroom with a one-inch-long stem and a stubby blue cap with white dots, and Bigwig is the four-inch-tall mushroom with a thin stem and a wide purple cap. The first one shrinks you, like the effect of a reduce spell, and the latter grows you, like the effect of an enlarge spell.

subject: pygmywort effect
fact: Pygmywort shrinks the consumer like a reduce spell, with a one-inch stem and stubby blue cap with white dots.
source_quote: Pygmywort is the mushroom with a one-inch-long stem and a stubby blue cap with white dots, and Bigwig is the four-inch-tall mushroom with a thin stem and a wide purple cap. The first one shrinks you, like the effect of a reduce spell...

subject: Ripplebark
fact: A fungus that tastes good when toasted. Collected by Daz as edible matter.

subject: ripplebark
fact: A mushroom that tastes good toasted; collected by Daz.
source_quote: ripplebark that tastes good toasted

subject: ripplebark property
fact: Ripplebark tastes good when toasted.
source_quote: He picks up some barrelstalk... ripplebark that tastes good toasted...

subject: Shal the advisor
fact: Shal is a mysterious new advisor to the Deep King, whose influence has caused the king to reject sage counsel.
source_quote: Shal, an advisor of his. Ever since they became friends, The Deep King has been unwilling to listen to any sage advice.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: stonespeaker crystal

source_quote: a 19 inch shard of quartz crystal... Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, and Speak with Plants... aids divinations

subject: Stonespeaker Crystal
fact: A 19-inch shard of quartz crystal gifted by Hgraam, capable of casting Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, and Speak with Plants, and enhancing divination spells. It is attuned to the voices of the stones and may serve as a conduit to the deeper truths of the Underdark, possibly even allowing communication with the crying rocks or the whispers of the Faerzress.
source_quote: “This is the stonespeaker crystal... it will also help you cast divinations.”

subject: Stonespeaker Crystal
fact: A 19-inch shard of quartz crystal gifted by Hgraam. It enables the spells Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, and Speak with Plants, and enhances divination magic. It is said to be attuned to the voices of the stones and the Underdark’s pain.
source_quote: This is the stonespeaker crystal, with it you can cast Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, and Speak with Plants. It will also help you cast divinations.

subject: stonespeaker crystal
fact: The stonespeaker crystal is a 19-inch shard of quartz crystal gifted by Hgraam that enables the spells Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, Speak with Plants, and enhances divination magic.
source_quote: His assistant brings a 19 inch shard of quartz crystal. ... “This is the stonespeaker crystal, with it you can cast Speak with Animals, Speak with the Dead, and Speak with Plants. It will also help you cast divinations.”

subject: timmask
fact: A two-foot-tall toadstool with orange and red stripes across its beige cap; uprooting it causes madness.
source_quote: A two-foot-tall toadstool with orange and red stripes across its beige cap known as “the devil’s mushroom,” or a timmask. Uprooting the mushroom can cause madness.

subject: Torchstalk
fact: A two-foot-tall mushroom with a combustible cap that burns for 24 hours when lit. Daz identifies it to Zalthir as a useful light source.

subject: torchstalk
fact: A two-foot-tall mushroom with a combustible cap that can burn for 24 hours when lit.
source_quote: Why, that’s a torchstalk. It has a combustible cap and can burn for 24 hours when lit.

subject: torchstalk property
fact: Torchstalk has a combustible cap and can burn for 24 hours when lit.
source_quote: Why, that’s a torchstalk. It has a combustible cap and can burn for 24 hours when lit.

subject: trillimac
fact: A mushroom that can be used for scrolls and makes a bread-like substance that can be rolled up; collected by Daz.
source_quote: trillimac that can be used for scrolls and makes a bread-like substance that can be rolled up

subject: Trillimac
fact: A mushroom usable for scrolls and that produces a bread-like substance that can be rolled up. Collected by Daz for magical and culinary purposes.

subject: trillimac property

fact: Perhaps something with a wider area of effect.
source_quote: or perhaps something with a wider area of effect.

subject: actor namesake
fact: Pelek was named after an actor, an unusual practice among Svirfneblin, raising questions about cultural influence, hidden ancestry, or magical legacy tied to performance or illusion.
source_quote: My mother named me after an actor.

subject: Blingdenstone’s Role
fact: Grygum insists that Blingdenstone is the party’s exit point and advises them to avoid references to Lolth, Menzoberranzan, and the number eight or spiders. This implies Blingdenstone has a political or religious stance opposed to those entities, and that the party’s journey beyond the cavern depends on navigating these taboos.
source_quote: The city of Blingdenstone is your exit. Make sure to deny any association to Lolth, or Menzoberranzan, and make any references to the number eight or spiders.

subject: Buppido’s Divine Mission
fact: Buppido’s conviction that he must return to save his people and his rage toward the Council of Savants imply a deeper, possibly prophetic, divine mission tied to the fate of the Derro, which may conflict with the group’s goals.
source_quote: The divine mission requires that I go back!

subject: Daz's spell strategy
fact: Daz is uncertain whether his spells are ineffective or if he needs to re-strategize, and no resolution is provided in this session.
source_quote: He feels a slight unease, wondering if his spells are just ineffective or if he needs to re-strategize

subject: Droki
fact: Pelek knows Droki works for the Council of Savants and is peculiar, but nothing more is known about him.
source_quote: I was told that he works for the Council of Savants. He’s very peculiar.

subject: Droki’s Magical Pace
fact: Droki moves with unnatural speed and precision, as if guided by magic or prophecy. His predictability makes him a courier, but his behavior suggests he is not acting of his own will. He may be a vessel, a puppet, or a living conduit for the corruption. His final leap into the fissure and the wisp of fog that follows imply planar or necromantic transit.
source_quote: “Droki also doesn’t seem to care if anyone is following him.”

subject: Droki’s True Purpose
fact: Droki’s unnaturally fast pace, disregard for observation, and ritualistic access to hidden passages suggest he is more than a courier—he may be bound to a divine or extraplanar force, and his route may lead to a greater secret in the Whorlstone Caverns.
source_quote: Droki also doesn’t seem to care if anyone is following him... He mutters to himself and to any Derro whom he says.

subject: Identity of the Humming Figure
fact: The hunched figure amid the spiral of corpses may be a derro cultist, a corrupted entity, or even a remnant of the Council of Savants; its purpose and connection to Droki or Buppido remain unknown.
source_quote: An off-key humming comes from a hunched figure working busily at something on the floor.

subject: ineffective spells
fact: Daz is questioning whether his spells are inherently ineffective or if he needs a re-strategized approach to dealing with the centipede swarm.
source_quote: He feels a slight unease, wondering if his spells are just ineffective or if he needs to re-strategize.

subject: Overbrighters
fact: A term used by Pelek with contempt, possibly referring to a faction or type of entity that overuses or misuses magical light sources. Its meaning is unexplained but implies a hidden conflict or cultural divide in the Underdark.

subject: Pelek’s Hand
fact: Pelek’s hand, bearing his obsidian ring, is missing and wandered off after his death. Its location is unknown, but it may be hidden in the fungal thicket, near the crack in the wall, or within the Black Pool. Retrieving it could yield the ring and possibly unlock further information about his death or the Council’s plans.
source_quote: Seems it went off scurrying about. There is a family ring on it, an obsidian ring of some value.

subject: Pelek’s name
fact: Pelek’s name is of uncertain origin, possibly derived from an actor or an onomatopoeic sound, but its true meaning is unstated and unresolved.
source_quote: ‘My mother named me after an actor. And well, there was always this doubt about the origin of the name and my lineage...'

subject: Pelek's origin
fact: Pelek’s name and lineage are shrouded in familial shame and uncertainty, stemming from his mother naming him after an actor, and his father’s jealousy — a mystery that may connect to deeper cultural or magical roots.
source_quote: There was always this doubt about the origin of the name and my lineage, which created a lot of friction in my family.

subject: Planar Breach Theory
fact: Daz has theorized that the Faerzress’s fluctuation may have broken the walls between planes, allowing entities from other dimensions to enter the Underdark. The ghost dismisses this as a ghost story, but the timing of Buppido’s madness, the Derro’s behavior, and the Faerzress’s anomaly suggest a deeper connection. The party has not yet investigated this possibility.
source_quote: Then if it blinked, could it have — I dunno — broken the walls between the planes?

subject: Planar Rupture
fact: The Faerzress anomaly may have temporarily broken the walls between planes, allowing extraplanar entities to enter the Underdark. Daz speculates this could explain the sudden madness of derro, the appearance of centipede swarms, and the ghostly persistence of Pelek. The party has not yet confirmed this theory, but it is a growing concern.
source_quote: Then if it blinked, could it have — I dunno — broken the walls between the planes?

subject: Shal
fact: Shal is the Deep King’s new advisor, but Hgraam has never met them.
source_quote: I have asked to meet Shal, but they refuse.

subject: spell strategy reconsideration
fact: Daz is actively reconsidering his spell selection and strategy, questioning whether his current spells are inadequate or if a different approach is needed.
source_quote: Maybe 'Burning Hands' would have been better?" he muses, or perhaps something with a wider area of effect. He feels a slight unease, wondering if his spells are just ineffective or if he needs to re-strategize.

subject: The Deep Gnomes as Path to the Dreamlands
fact: The Deep Gnomes are the only viable route to the Dreamlands, as confirmed by Hgraam, and their city is the key to navigating the Underdark’s hidden pathways.
source_quote: Thorin learns from Hgraam that the best way to the Dreamlands is through the city of the Deep gnomes.

subject: The Demons of Valkenvylve and Beholder of Spidersilk
fact: The demons observed at Valkenvylve, the Beholder in the Spidersilk caves, the demonic manta rays, and Demogorgon are not isolated events but manifestations of a single, growing magical rupture in the Underdark.
source_quote: Zalthir turns to Thorin, “The Stone Giant is particularly attuned to the rocks? So what we have seen as localized appearances of demons is not localized. The demons at Valkenvylve, the Beholder in the Spidersilk caves, the demonic manta rays, and Demogorgon, all of this is no coincidence.”

subject: The Earth Rejects Its Wards
fact: This portent implies that ancient magical protections—wards, seals, or divine barriers—placed long ago to contain evil beneath Gracklstugh have failed or been corrupted. It suggests the evil is not merely spreading, but actively breaking free from containment, and may be tied to the Deep King’s loss of control or Shal’s hidden agenda.
source_quote: “The earth rejects its wards, and the tunnels shake in fury.”

subject: The Faerzress
fact: The nature of the Faerzress is unknown, and whether its blink broke plane barriers is an unresolved mystery.
source_quote: No one knows what the Faerzress is. And so I assumed it was something that happens.

subject: The Faerzress
fact: Thorin wonders if the Faerzress affects his sanity and is connected to the spreading madness.
source_quote: Thorin wonders if this has anything to do with the Faerzress, which has affects his sanity.

subject: The Faerzress and Sanity
fact: The Faerzress, the magical radiation of the Underdark, is implied to be weakening the sanity of those exposed to it, possibly linking it to the madness spreading from the blackest depths.
source_quote: Thorin wonders if this has anything to do with the Faerzress, which has affects his sanity.

subject: The Faerzress and Sanity
fact: The Faerzress, the magical radiation of the Underdark, is increasingly affecting the sanity of those who dwell within it. Thorin wonders if it is connected to the demonic incursions and the madness of the Derro. It may be amplifying or even causing the corruption, acting as a psychic amplifier for the evil stirring below.
source_quote: “Thorin wonders if this has anything to do with the Faerzress, which has affects his sanity.”

subject: The Faerzress Connection
fact: Thorin suspects the Faerzress — the magical radiation that affects sanity in the Underdark — may be amplifying or intertwined with the current corruption. If true, this could mean the madness spreading through the Underdark is not just external, but a resonance of the land’s own psychic decay.
source_quote: Thorin wonders if this has anything to do with the Faerzress, which has affects his sanity.

subject: The Grey Ghosts
fact: The Deep King has become paranoid since Shal became his advisor, and his former calmness is gone.
source_quote: He and I would watch the stones grow. But something has happened to him. He has become paranoid towards old and new friends.

subject: The Grey Ghosts
fact: The Grey Ghosts are entities created by the Deep King as enemies to justify his paranoia, and their existence reflects the psychological unraveling of his rule.
source_quote: Grey Ghosts? The Deep King creates so many enemies. He used to be so calm. He and I would watch the stones grow. But something has happened to him. He has become paranoid towards old and new friends.

subject: The Grey Ghosts
fact: The Grey Ghosts are mysterious entities referenced by Hgraam as creations of the Deep King, possibly spectral enforcers or failed experiments. Their existence suggests the Deep King has been experimenting with necromantic or psionic control methods — a sign of his descent into desperation and paranoia.
source_quote: Grey Ghosts? The Deep King creates so many enemies. He used to be so calm. He and I would watch the stones grow. But something has happened to him. He has become paranoid towards old and new friends.

subject: The Identity of Shal
fact: Shal is an unknown entity who has insidiously gained the Deep King’s trust and corrupted his judgment. Their refusal to meet with Hgraam and their sudden influence suggest they are not a typical advisor — possibly a demon, a fey, a construct, or something older and more alien.
source_quote: I have asked to meet Shal, but they refuse.

subject: The Identity of Shal
fact: Shal’s refusal to meet anyone, combined with their sudden influence over the Deep King and the timing of the corruption’s acceleration, suggests they are not a normal being. They may be a demon, a fragment of the Faerzress given sentience, a long-dead entity returned, or an avatar of the evil stirring below. Their identity is the key to stopping the collapse.
source_quote: “I have asked to meet Shal, but they refuse.”

subject: The Missing Hand
fact: Grygum’s hand, bearing an obsidian family ring, is missing and may have wandered away after his death. He claims it went 'off scurrying about,' suggesting supernatural autonomy. The party has not searched for it, but its recovery may yield clues to his identity, Buppido’s motives, or the nature of the ring.
source_quote: There is a family ring on it, an obsidian ring of some value. You can keep it if you find the hand.

subject: The Nature of the Underdark’s Corruption
fact: A pervasive, growing evil is spreading through the Underdark, manifesting as madness, demonic incursions, and sentient rock suffering. The cause is unknown but appears tied to the Sundering and possibly the Faerzress. The stones themselves warn of portents: caves with two faces, devoured rock, overgrown land, and shaking tunnels.
source_quote: Something evil stirs in the Underdark. The rock itself cries in pain and horror, and a madness creeps from the blackest depths. Pay heed to the signs surrounding you. A cave with two faces. Rock devoured, and the land overgrown. The pebble believes itself flesh. The earth rejects its wards, and the tunnels shake in fury.

subject: The Overbrighters
fact: Pelek repeatedly refers to the party as 'Overbrighters,' a term of derision or cultural distinction. It implies the party originates from or is associated with the surface world or a region beyond the Underdark. The term may be linked to the Council of Savants’ propaganda, or it may reflect a deeper societal divide between surface-dwellers and Underdark natives.
source_quote: The ghost sighs, 'Look, I don’t want to possess you. It’s awkward. And frankly, I like you. The city of Blingdenstone is your exit. There are many routes to the Overbrite from there.'

subject: The Pebble Believes Itself Flesh
fact: Another of Hgraam’s portents, this phrase suggests that something in the Underdark has achieved a blasphemous state of sentience—minerals or stone have become animate, or living beings have been fused with rock. It may be connected to the stonespeaker crystal, Buppido’s shrine, or the nature of the Faerzress itself.
source_quote: “The pebble believes itself flesh.”

subject: The Tiny Tunnel
fact: A narrow, unexplored tunnel behind a crack in the wall of Grygum, visible only to Pelek’s ghost. It is too small for humans to pass, but may be traversable by small creatures or through magical means. Pelek claims it leads to the 'whorlstone tunnels,' suggesting a deeper, hidden network connected to the Council of Savants or other Underdark factions.
source_quote: A tiny tunnel. Tiny all the way through.

subject: The Two-Faced Cave
fact: Hgraam’s prophecy mentions a ‘cave with two faces’ as a sign of evil’s presence. This may refer to the fissure used by Droki, the shrine of Buppido, or a deeper location yet to be found. It is a key portent that must be interpreted, possibly indicating a portal, a duality of reality, or a hidden entity that exists in two states at once.
source_quote: “A cave with two faces. Rock devoured, and the land overgrown.”

subject: The Two-Faced Cave
fact: The portent of the cave with two faces, the rock devoured, the land overgrown, the pebble believing itself flesh, and the tunnels shaking in fury are recurring omens that mark the presence of evil’s face in the Underdark.
source_quote: A cave with two faces. Rock devoured, and the land overgrown. The pebble believes itself flesh. The earth rejects its wards, and the tunnels shake in fury.

subject: Whispering Fungal Thicket
fact: The hissing sound of wind through the fungal thicket is mistaken for uncounted whispering voices. Daz is unnerved, Thorin suspects psychedelics, Pelek dismisses it as natural — leaving the true nature of the sound unresolved and eerie.

subject: Why Only Blindness?
fact: Zalthir is troubled that his monastic order taught him to make others blind, not silent — a fundamental mismatch with their stated purpose. The reason behind this corrupted training remains unknown.

subject: Zalthir’s Monastic Silence
fact: Zalthir’s monastic order taught him how to blind others but not how to silence them, leaving him unprepared for the constant chatter of the party and the ghost. His frustration suggests a deeper spiritual or philosophical conflict — perhaps his order’s teachings are incomplete, or the Underdark demands a different kind of discipline.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders why a monastic order devoted to silence only taught him how to make people blind, and not how to make them silent.
